Nelson Mandela: President of South Africa from 1994 to 1999.
Known as 'Light of the Faith,' this Zengid dynasty ruler governed Seljuk Syria from 1146 to 1174 and looms large in the history of the Second Crusade — who was he?
Nur al-Din Zengi: Emir of Aleppo (1146–1174) and Damascus (1154–1174)
The first prime minister of India from the south, he steered the country's 1991 economic liberalisation after previously serving as chief minister of Andhra Pradesh — who is he?
P. V. Narasimha Rao: Prime Minister of India from 1991 to 1996.
A four-star general who staged a 1999 coup against Nawaz Sharif's government, this military officer went on to serve as Pakistan's president from 2001 to 2008 — who was he?

Pervez Musharraf: President of Pakistan from 2001 to 2008. Pervez Musharraf (11 August 1943 – 5 February 2023) was a Pakistani politician and military officer who served as the tenth president of Pakistan from 2001 to 2008.
This act of deliberate communication with a deity — through hymns, incantations, or spontaneous words — has been documented in written sources for some five thousand years — what is it called?
Prayer: Invocation or act that seeks to activate a rapport with a deity.

Serving as India's president from 2017 to 2022, he was the first person from Uttar Pradesh and the first member of the Bharatiya Janata Party to hold that office, after serving as Governor of Bihar — who is he?
Ram Nath Kovind: President of India from 2017 to 2022.

Fought from 1921 to 1926, this conflict pitted Spain and later France against Berber guerrillas led by Abd el-Krim in northern Morocco, and saw history's first amphibious landing to use tanks and aircraft — which conflict?
Rif War: 1921–1926 war between Spain and Riffian tribes of Morocco.
Founded by a Varangian prince who settled at Novgorod in 862, this noble lineage ruled Kievan Rus' and, through its Moscow branch, the tsars of Russia until 1598 — what dynasty was it?
Rurikids: Noble lineage and rulers of Kievan Rus'. The Rurikids were the ruling dynasty of Kievan Rus' and its principalities following its disintegration.
After leaving office, she traded the Finnish prime minister's chair for a desk at the Tony Blair Institute, advising on leadership reform — which young Social Democrat was she?
Sanna Marin: Prime Minister of Finland from 2019 to 2023.
Serving as Argentina's Minister of Economy from 2022 to 2023, this politician had earlier been Chief of Cabinet under Cristina Fernández de Kirchner and twice mayor of Tigre — who is he?
Sergio Massa: Argentine politician and lawyer (born 1972)
A media tycoon worth $6.8 billion at his death, which Italian served as prime minister across three separate governments between 1994 and 2011?
Silvio Berlusconi: Italian media tycoon and politician (1936–2023)
The first Louisianian to serve as House majority whip since the early 1970s, he has represented Louisiana's 1st congressional district since 2008 — who is he?

Emphasizing harmony with an enigmatic guiding force behind reality, this Chinese philosophical and religious tradition promotes effortless action, simplicity, and the three treasures of compassion, frugality, and humility — which tradition?
Taoism: Religious and philosophical tradition. Taoism or Daoism is a philosophical and religious tradition indigenous to China, emphasizing harmony with the Tao 道.
Cao Wei, Shu Han and Eastern Wu carved up China between 220 and 280 AD after the collapse of the Han dynasty — what is this era called?
Three Kingdoms: Period of Chinese history from 220 to 280 CE.

Political theorist Roger Griffin traced this extreme, supremacist strain of national pride — an ideological foundation beneath Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany — to the view of nations as living organisms with 'great cultural destinies.' What's it called?
A two-time Chief Minister of Maharashtra who also served as India's Minister of Earth Sciences, this Indian National Congress politician hailed from the Latur district — who is he?
A rags-to-riches Western Han general celebrated for his campaigns against the Xiongnu, he rose through ties to Emperor Wu and was uncle to the famed general Huo Qubing — who was he?
After serving as a concubine and then empress, this woman founded her own short-lived Zhou dynasty to become the only undisputed female sovereign in China's history — who was she?
Wu Zetian: Empress regnant of China from 690 to 705.
Revered as the Father of the Nation, this ruler of Abu Dhabi became the first president of a newly unified Gulf federation in 1971?
Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan: President of the United Arab Emirates from 1971 to 2004.
Which of these people was born first?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Frank Oppenheimer is a physicist. The younger brother of renowned physicist J.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Émilie du Châtelet is a mathematician. It circulated widely, generated heated debates, and was translated into German and Italian in 1743.
What is the atomic number of Hassium?
Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
What is the atomic number of Krypton?
Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.
In what year was Alfred Nobel born?
Alfred Nobel: Alfred Bernhard Nobel ( noh-BEL; Swedish: [ˈǎlːfrɛd nʊˈbɛlː]; 21 October 1833 – 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.
In what year was Kitty Oppenheimer born?
Kitty Oppenheimer: Robert Oppenheimer, the director of the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos Laboratory during World War II.
In what year was John Maynard Keynes born?
John Maynard Keynes: Keynes was educated at King's College at the University of Cambridge, where he graduated in 1904 with a B.A. in mathematics.
In what year did Thales of Miletus die?
Thales of Miletus: Thales of Miletus ( THAY-leez; Ancient Greek: Θαλῆς; c. 626/623 – c. 548/545 BC) was an Ancient Greek pre-Socratic philosopher from Miletus in Ionia, Asia Minor.
In what year did Ernest Rutherford die?
Ernest Rutherford: Together with Thomas Royds, Rutherford is credited with proving that alpha radiation is composed of helium nuclei.
In what year was Aluminium discovered?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
Which company manufactures Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: Skunk Works. The SR-71 was developed in the 1960s as a black project by Lockheed's Skunk Works division.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 from?

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Soviet Union. The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 (Russian: Микоян и Гуревич МиГ-19; NATO reporting name: Farmer) is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Pyxis?
Pyxis: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pyxis is a small and faint constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Neodymium?
Neodymium: Carl Auer von Welsbach. Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
Who is credited with discovering TON 618?
Who is credited with discovering Thallium?
Thallium: Claude-Auguste Lamy. Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.

Produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex, this mineralocorticoid is the body's key sodium-saver, quietly governing blood pressure and potassium balance in the kidney — which hormone is it?
Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.
This deep-tissue swelling — of the face, tongue, throat, or limbs — comes on within minutes to hours and is driven by either histamine or bradykinin — what is it?
Angioedema is an area of swelling (edema) of the lower layer of skin and tissue just under the skin or mucous membranes.
With almost 500 species in the daisy family, this large plant genus includes mugwort, wormwood, and sagebrush, and is sometimes confused with a related genus of sages — which genus?
Artemisia (plant) (art--) is a large, diverse genus of plants belonging to the daisy family, Asteraceae, with almost 500 species.
Which SI unit of radioactivity honors the scientist who co-discovered the phenomenon alongside the Curies?
Becquerel (symbol: Bq) is the unit of radioactivity in the International System of Units (SI).
Composed mostly of plasma along with red cells, white cells, and platelets, this body fluid ferries oxygen and nutrients to cells while hauling waste away — name the fluid?

Blood is a body fluid in the circulatory system of humans and other vertebrates that delivers necessary substances such as nutrients and oxygen to the cells of the body, and transports metabolic waste products away from those same cells.
The only living group in its tribe, this genus of over 250 fuzzy bees forms small colonies under a single queen — and unlike honeybees, its females can sting again and again — what is it?
Bumblebee (or bumble bee, bumble-bee, or humble-bee) is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, part of Apidae, one of the bee families.

This quaternary ammonium compound ferries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for energy production, and is concentrated in heart and skeletal muscle, though most people synthesize enough on their own. What is it called?
Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound involved in metabolism in most mammals, plants, and some bacteria.
Often preceded by a gallbladder attack and typically caused by a gallstone lodging in the cystic duct, which condition can progress to complications like gallstone pancreatitis?
Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder. Often gallbladder attacks (biliary colic) precede acute cholecystitis.
Native to Asia but so invasive in Australian cities that it was dubbed 'Most Important Pest/Problem' in 2008, which urban-adapted bird species is this?
Common myna (Acridotheres tristis), sometimes spelled mynah, is a bird in the family Sturnidae, native to Asia.
A bright yellow polyphenol found in turmeric, a member of the ginger family, this compound is sold as an herbal supplement, cosmetic ingredient, food flavoring, and food coloring — which compound?
Curcumin is a bright yellow chemical produced by the plant species Curcuma longa.

Occurring five times in the phrase 'no highway cowboys,' this linguistic term describes two vowel sounds gliding together within a single syllable, contrasting with a single steady vowel sound — what is it?
Diphthong (DIP-), also known as a gliding vowel or a vowel glide, is a combination of two adjacent vowel sounds within the same syllable.
This is the only surviving member of its order, the Proboscidea, and its tusks are actually overgrown incisor teeth used as both weapons and tools — what animal is it?
Elephant are the largest living land animals.
Aerobic exercise, laughter, dancing, and romantic love can all induce this intense feeling of well-being — which is also, less happily, a symptom of mania — what state is it?
Euphoria (yoo-) is the experience (or affect) of pleasure or excitement and intense feelings of well-being and happiness.
Systematically named methanal and carrying the formula CH2O, this pungent gas turns up in particle board, disinfectants, and lab specimen jars — what is it?

Formaldehyde (for-, US also fr-) (systematic name methanal) is a pungent colorless gas mainly used in the production of industrial resins, such as for particle board, coatings, plastics, pulp, paper, synthetic fibers, and textiles.
Nicknamed 'The Lawyer' and celebrated for his eccentric style, this principal shareholder controlled over 4% of Italy's entire GDP through his automaker — who was he?
Gianni Agnelli (12 March 1921 - 24 January 2003), nicknamed L'Avvocato ('The Lawyer'), was an Italian industrialist and principal shareholder of Fiat.
A retrovirus that gradually dismantles the human immune system, it leads to AIDS and, untreated, shortens life by roughly a decade — what is it?
HIV (HIVs) are two species of Lentivirus (a subgroup of retrovirus) that infect humans.
First unearthed in 1994 in Spain's Gran Dolina cave, this Early Pleistocene human was named 'pioneer man' because it was among the first to settle Western Europe. Which species is it?

Homo antecessor (Latin for 'pioneer man') is an extinct species of archaic human recorded in the Spanish Sierra de Atapuerca, a productive archaeological site, from 1.2 to 0.8 million years ago during the Early Pleistocene.
More than 20 types make up this genetic skin condition, whose Greek-derived name means "fish" — a nod to its hallmark dry, thickened, scaly texture — which disorder?
Ichthyosis is a family of genetic skin disorders characterized by dry, thickened, scaly skin.
This 17th-century Dutch microscopist proved that an insect's egg, larva, pupa, and adult are all one creature, and in 1658 became the first to observe and describe red blood cells — who was he?
Jan Swammerdam (February 12, 1637 - February 17, 1680) was a Dutch biologist and microscopist.
A founder of modern geometric analysis, this American mathematician won the 2019 Abel Prize for pioneering work in geometric PDEs and gauge theory — who is she?
Karen Uhlenbeck (born August 24, 1942) is an American mathematician and one of the founders of modern geometric analysis.

A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange believed to have originated in northeastern India around the 1st millennium BC, this small evergreen citrus tree bears a tart yellow fruit used worldwide — name the fruit?
Lemon (Citrus limon) is a species of small evergreen tree in the Citrus genus of the flowering plant family Rutaceae.
Named for a Dutch physicist, this six-parameter family of linear equations converts spacetime coordinates between reference frames moving at constant relative velocity — what is it?
Lorentz transformation are a six-parameter family of linear transformations from a coordinate frame in spacetime to another frame that moves at a constant velocity relative to the former.

A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered a new element in 1939 by purifying lanthanum laced with actinium, and went on to become the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Marguerite Perey (19 October 1909 - 13 May 1975) was a French physicist and a student of Marie Curie.
This hedge fund manager and licensed physician was among the first to predict and profit from the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis, later portrayed on screen in The Big Short. Who is he?
Michael Burry (born June 19, 1971) is an American investor, hedge fund manager, and licensed physician.
An Austrian-School economist who called the state 'robbery systematized and writ large,' he founded and championed anarcho-capitalism across more than twenty books — who was he?
Murray Rothbard (March 2, 1926 - January 7, 1995) was an American economist of the Austrian School, economic historian, political theorist, and activist.

Found across 26 African countries in lakes, rivers and swamps — with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana — adult males of this reptile can stretch past five meters; what is it?
Nile crocodile (Crocodylus niloticus) is a large crocodilian native to freshwater habitats in Africa, where it is present in 26 countries.
Also covering the modification of facial growth known as dentofacial orthopedics, this branch of dentistry corrects mal-positioned teeth and bite patterns. What field is it?

Orthodontics (also referred to as orthodontia) is a dentistry specialty that addresses the diagnosis, prevention, management, and correction of mal-positioned teeth and jaws, as well as misaligned bite patterns.
Made by grinding dry-roasted legumes and often tweaked with salt or emulsifiers, this protein-rich spread is the most popular of all the nut butters — what is it?
Peanut butter is a food paste or spread made from ground, dry-roasted peanuts.

Enclosed in a papery husk formed from its calyx, the fruit of this nightshade-family genus tastes like a firm tomato crossed with a sweet, tangy grape — nearly half of its species grow only in Mexico. Name the genus?
Physalis (from Ancient) is a genus of approximately 75 to 90 flowering plants in the nightshade family (Solanaceae), which are native to the Americas and Australasia.
This autonomic nervous system disorder causes an abnormally large jump in heart rate — thirty beats per minute within ten minutes — simply from sitting up or standing. What condition is it?
Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is a condition characterized by an abnormally large increase in heart rate upon sitting up or standing.
Easily identified by its striking red and black coloring, this common European insect is often mistaken for an unrelated lookalike called the cinnamon bug — what insect is it?
Pyrrhocoris apterus is a common insect of the family Pyrrhocoridae.

An emeritus fellow of an Oxford college and the first-ever holder of a professorship for the public understanding of science, this British evolutionary biologist is also known as a prominent atheist author — who is he?
Richard Dawkins (born 26 March 1941) is a British evolutionary biologist, zoologist, science communicator, noted atheist, and author.
This Indian-American executive succeeded Steve Ballmer as CEO of a major tech company in 2014 after running its cloud and enterprise division — who is he?
Satya Nadella (born 19 August 1967) is an Indian-American business executive.

Built for the Marine Corps by adding a third engine and a seventh main rotor blade to an earlier heavy-lift helicopter, this aircraft entered service in 1981 and flies from Navy ships — which helicopter?
Sikorsky CH-53E Super Stallion is a heavy lift helicopter operated by the United States military.
Doctors examine the color of this coughed-up airway mucus — greenish or yellow tints can hint at infection, though not which organism caused it — what is it?
Sputum is mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways (the trachea and bronchi).
This Turkish businesswoman served as one of her father's chief advisers back in 2013, when he held the office of prime minister and later became Turkey's president — who is she?
Sümeyye Erdoğan (ne Erdoan; born 22 August 1985) is a Turkish businesswoman and the daughter of President Recep Tayyip Erdoan.
This genus of coniferous evergreen in the cypress family includes five species — two native to North America, three to eastern Asia — and is sister to the genus Thujopsis. Name the genus?
Thuja is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).

This flowering plant in the ginger family is native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, requiring temperatures between 68 and 86°F and high rainfall. Its rhizomes are gathered and can be used fresh or dried for consumption and dyeing — what is it?
Turmeric is a flowering plant in the ginger family Zingiberaceae. Turmeric powder has a warm, bitter, black pepper-like flavor and earthy, mustard-like aroma.
This pungent Japanese condiment, ground from the rhizome of a plant related to horseradish and mustard, traditionally accompanies sushi. What is it?
A white, water-insoluble powder with the formula ZnO, this compound turns up in everything from sunscreens and calamine lotion to batteries and semiconductors — name this compound?
Zinc oxide is an inorganic compound with the formula ZnO. Although it occurs naturally as the mineral zincite, most zinc oxide is produced synthetically.
Made by the adrenal glands, this hormone powers the fight-or-flight response — boosting blood flow to muscles, dilating pupils and raising blood sugar by hitting alpha and beta receptors. What is it?
Adrenaline: Hormone and medication. It appears as a white microcrystalline granule.
Called lucerne in the UK, Australia and New Zealand, this perennial legume has been grown as livestock fodder since ancient times — which plant?
Alfalfa: Plant species in pea family.
A member of the aminopenicillin class, this oral antibiotic is a go-to for ear infections, strep throat, and pneumonia — and is often paired with clavulanic acid. What is it?
NATO code-named 'Condor,' this Soviet-designed four-engine giant is the largest military transport aircraft still flying today — which aircraft?

Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Soviet military transport aircraft. Assembly of the first aircraft begun in 1979; the An-124 (which was sometimes referred to as the An-40 in the West) performed its maiden flight on 24 December 1982.
Writing in 499 CE that he was 23 years old, this pioneering Indian scholar's explicit discussion of the relativity of motion marks him as an early physicist too — who was he?
Native to the steppes of Central Asia, this two-humped pack animal's cold and drought tolerance made it indispensable to Silk Road caravans — what is it?
Bactrian camel: Species of mammal of Asia.
This steroid medication treats everything from rheumatoid arthritis to psoriasis, and can even be given to speed a premature baby's lung development before birth — what is it?
Betamethasone: Steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.
Launched as the 7X7 program in 1978 and designed to complement the larger 747, which American wide-body airliner first entered service with United Airlines in 1982?
Too small to fuse hydrogen but massive enough to briefly burn deuterium, these objects between 13 and 80 Jupiter masses cool over time through spectral classes M, L, T, and Y — what are they called?
With more than 220 species and over 26,000 registered cultivars, this flowering plant genus includes the very species whose leaves are processed into tea worldwide — which genus?
Camellia: Genus of flowering plants in the tea family.
A woody shrub native to South America, this starchy tuber yields tapioca and, when grated and toasted, becomes Brazil's farofa and West Africa's garri — what crop is it?
Cassava: Staple crop. Although a perennial plant, cassava is extensively cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions as an annual crop for its edible starchy tuberous root.
Known by the common name 'greater celandine,' this perennial flowering plant belongs to the poppy family and is native to Europe and western Asia — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family. One of two species in the genus Chelidonium, it is native to Europe and western Asia and introduced widely in North America.
Dubbed the 'father of information theory,' this polymath was the first to apply Boolean algebra to digital circuits and helped found the field of artificial intelligence — who is he?

A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa, this bird tricks other species into raising its young by laying eggs that mimic the host's, and even disguises itself as a hawk — what bird is it?
Common cuckoo: Species of bird. It is a brood parasite, which means it lays eggs in the nests of other bird species, particularly of dunnocks, meadow pipits, and reed warblers.

This blood-feeding parasitic insect, scientifically Pthirus pubis, typically lives in coarse body hair and diverged from a gorilla-infecting relative about 3.3 million years ago — what is it commonly called?
Crab louse: Species of insect. The crab louse or pubic louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
This Swedish tech entrepreneur founded and chairs a streaming giant, with a net worth estimated at $8.7 billion in December 2025 — who is he?
This bodily process breaks large food molecules into water-soluble components through both mechanical action like chewing and chemical action from enzymes — what's it called?
Digestion: Biological process of breaking down food.
Sometimes nicknamed 'math dyslexia' even though it's a distinct condition, this learning disorder involves persistent difficulty understanding numbers and performing calculations — what is it called?
This Italian-American physicist discovered two elements, technetium and astatine, plus the antiproton — the last earning him a share of the 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was he?
Emilio Segrè: Italian-American nuclear physicist and radiochemist (1905–1989)
Marketed under brand names like Arcoxia, this selective COX-2 inhibitor developed by Merck was approved in 63 countries by 2007 — everywhere, notably, except the United States — what is the drug?
In this common vision condition, distant objects appear sharp but close-up objects blur because light focuses behind the retina instead of on it - what is it?
Farsightedness: Eye condition in which light is focused behind instead of on the retina.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive that several 19th-century chemists died or were injured trying to isolate it, until Henri Moissan finally succeeded in 1886 — which element?
Fluorine: Chemical element with atomic number 9 (F)
Born in Pisa in 1564, this Italian polymath has been crowned the father of observational astronomy and the scientific method — and was among the earliest tinkerers to build a thermoscope. Who is he?
Galileo Galilei: Italian physicist and astronomer (1564–1642)
Despite centuries of use in Korean and Chinese traditional medicine, no clinical evidence supports health claims for this Panax-genus root, often sold as a dietary supplement — what is it?
Ginseng: Root of a plant used in herbal preparations.
This junctional area between the torso and thigh, where the lower abdominal wall meets the leg, is commonly strained in a familiar sports injury — what is it called?
Groin: Area between the torso and the thigh. In human anatomy, the groin, also known as the inguinal region or iliac region, is the junctional area between the torso and the thigh.
This wingless insect spends its entire life on the human scalp, sipping blood, and can neither fly nor jump — its short stumpy legs can't even walk well on a flat surface. What tiny freeloader is it?
Head louse: Insect parasite of humans.
This academic discipline studies the methods, sources, and interpretive approaches historians use when writing about the past — what's it called?
Historiography: Study of the methods used by historians.
A yellow-flowered perennial whose leaves look perforated by translucent glands, this plant is famed in folklore and traditional medicine under a saintly common name — what is its botanical name?
Hypericum perforatum: Flowering plant in the St John's wort family.
Endemic to semiarid central-eastern Australia and also called the "fierce snake," this elapid was rediscovered in 1972 after nearly 90 years of obscurity — what is it?
Inland taipan: Extremely venomous snake native to Australia.

This Dutch microscopist showed that an insect's egg, larva, pupa, and adult are all one animal, pioneered the microscope in dissections, and in 1658 became the first to observe red blood cells — who was he?
Jan Swammerdam: Dutch biologist and microscopist (1637–1680)
Equal to the work done when a one-newton force moves an object one metre, this SI unit of energy is named for a 19th-century English physicist — which unit?
Joule: SI unit of energy. The joule ( JOOL, or JOWL; symbol: J) is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).
Living as a recluse in a log house outside Kaluga, this Russian pioneer of rocket science inspired both Wernher von Braun and the architects of the Soviet space program — who is he?
Also known as Peruvian ginseng, this Andean root crop is grown at high altitude in Peru and Bolivia and exported worldwide as a dietary powder — what plant is it?
Lepidium meyenii: Plant species native to South America.
This American WWII twin-engine, twin-boom fighter carried its pilot alone in a central nacelle and served as fighter-bomber, night fighter, and long-range escort — which aircraft was it?
Lockheed P-38 Lightning: American twin-engined fighter of WWII. The Lockheed P-38 Lightning is an American single-seat, twin-engined fighter aircraft that was used during World War II.
Occurring naturally as the mineral brucite, this poorly soluble white solid neutralizes stomach acid in a well-known antacid — which compound?
Magnesium hydroxide: Inorganic compound of formula Mg(OH)2.
Among the first women in Canada to earn a medical doctorate, this physician-chemist is best known for her 1913 work with Leonor Michaelis on enzyme kinetics — who was she?
Maud Menten: Canadian physician and chemist (1879–1960)
Marketed under brand names like Quaalude and Sopor, this sedative was pulled from commercial production in the mid-1980s due to widespread misuse — which drug?

A hemiparasitic plant that taps into its host tree via a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, its European species was introduced to Northern California in 1900 — what plant is it?
Mistletoe: Common name for various parasitic plants.
Its Inuktitut name means 'the bearded one,' and males emit a strong odor during rut to attract mates — which thick-coated Arctic mammal is this?
Muskox: Species of arctic land mammal.
Popularized by neurologist George Beard in the 1860s, this diagnosis described fatigue, anxiety, and heart palpitations often blamed on the stresses of modern life — what was the condition called?
This biochemical process lets an organism turn food and water into energy and building blocks, and can go wrong with too much or too little of certain essential substances — what process?
Nutrition: Provision to cells and organisms to support life.
In young children it can mean ear-pulling, extra crying, and poor sleep; it's a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear, from acute infections to lingering fluid. What's the medical name?
Otitis media: Inflammation of the middle ear. One of the two main types is acute otitis media (AOM), an infection of rapid onset that usually presents with ear pain.
Cultivated across the tropics for its fragrant essential oil, over 90% of this mint-family herb's global oil supply now comes from Indonesia — which plant?
What is the process by which immune cells like macrophages and neutrophils engulf pathogens and debris with their plasma membrane, forming an internal compartment called a phagosome?
Phagocytosis: Cell membrane engulfing a large particle.
Used in randomized clinical trials as a genuine-looking but pharmacologically inert stand-in — like a sugar pill or saline shot — what's this sham treatment called?
Placebo: Substance or treatment of no therapeutic value.
This rare genetic disorder linked to chromosome 15 leaves affected children constantly hungry, often leading to obesity, alongside a narrow forehead and small hands and feet — what is it?
Prader–Willi syndrome: Genetic disorder involving an imprinted genomic region.
This term covers the laws, regulations, and government actions that address issues from education to healthcare to transportation — what is it?
Public policy: Government proposals, principles and actions.
Found in the Atlas Mountains as the only member of its family native to Africa, this large ruminant's males are called stags and females are hinds — what species is it?
Red deer: Species of hoofed mammal.

This interdisciplinary field combines a power source, mechanical construction, control circuits, and software to design machines that assist humans in fields from medicine to space exploration — what is it?
Robotics: Design, construction, use, and application of robots.
Native to Mexico and Guatemala, this mint-family plant is prized for its hydrophilic seeds known as chia — what's its scientific name?
Salvia hispanica: Species of flowering plant in the mint family.
Located between the bladder and the rectum in male mammals, this paired accessory gland produces most of the fluid released during ejaculation — what is it?
Seminal vesicles: Pair of simple tubular glands.

A parasomnia in which wakefulness and deep non-REM sleep occur in different brain regions at once, this condition can produce anything from bathroom trips to attempts at cooking or even driving — what is it?
Sleepwalking: Sleeping phenomenon combined with wakefulness.

Synthesized by Aristotle and taken as fact for two millennia, this superseded theory held that maggots could arise straight from dead flesh, until Louis Pasteur helped discredit it — what was it called?
Spontaneous generation: Theory of life arising from non-living matter.
Born from Russia's PAK FA programme begun in 1999 and carrying the internal name T-50, this twin-engine jet was the first Russian military aircraft built with stealth technology — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russian stealth multirole fighter aircraft.
From Greek for 'arrangement' and 'method', this science names and classifies organisms into ranked groups — domain, kingdom, phylum, and on down to species — what is the field?
